kanainagar-temple.desc: At Kanainagar, near Mohammadpur, Sitaram built a Krishna temple in the five-pinnacled pancharatna style. Weathered brick and fragments of terracotta show its former quality. It sits in a rural setting, often with children and goats around it. Combine it with the palace ruins.
blocks: How to get there
A short van or bike ride west of the Mohammadpur ruins.
Good to know
Ask for directions in Mohammadpur bazar; signage is limited.

glance: Approx. 10–20 BDT per piece at stalls
Evening pitha stalls around Magura town
magura-winter-pitha.desc: In the cold months, homes and roadside stalls make rice-flour cakes filled or soaked with new date gur. Bhapa pitha is steamed in small pots with coconut and gur inside. Chitoi pitha comes with hot gur syrup, and patishapta are thin crepes rolled around sweet filling. Look for stalls near bus stands and bazars in the evening.

gachhi-date-palm-tapping.desc: Gachhis are the specialists who prepare and tap date palms. Before winter they scrape the trunk, then each evening cut a fresh face and hang a clay pot beneath a bamboo spout. At dawn they climb down with the sweet raw sap, part of which is drunk fresh and the rest boiled into gur. The craft is passed down in families and is slowly declining.
blocks: Good to know
Watch at dawn in any village; raw sap can carry the Nipah virus, so prefer boiled gur over drinking unboiled juice.

glance: 165 km to Magura by road, 4–6 hours by bus or car
chhandra-zamindar-bari.desc: Chhandra is a village in Talkhari union of Shalikha upazila. The estate was held by the Dev Roy family; the founder, Alongkhon Mohon Dev Roy, had no children, and the last zamindar, Abani Mohon Dev Roy, died in 1973. The family kept elephants that were tied up near the Bagabati river and in 1957 started a primary school that still runs. Today parts of the house stand half lost in the trees, along with a Durga temple, a Kali shrine and the zamindars' pond.
blocks: How to get there
Go from Magura town to Shalikha or Arpara by bus, then take a CNG or easy-bike to Chhandra village in Talkhari union.
Good to know
There are no facilities; go in daylight, wear proper shoes for the undergrowth and keep away from loose walls.

glance: Village haats around Magura town and Shalikha
magura-khejur-gur.desc: Magura shares the south-west's date palm tradition, and in winter its villages produce liquid jhola gur and set patali. The flavour depends on cold nights and careful boiling. Locals eat it with muri, flattened rice or warm pitha. Buying straight from a village maker is the best way to get pure gur.

glance: 165 km to Magura by road, 4–6 hours by bus or car
farrukh-ahmad-birthplace.desc: Farrukh Ahmad, known for his poems drawing on Islamic and maritime imagery such as 'Sath Sagorer Majhi', was born in Majhail village in Sreepur in 1918. His birthplace is listed among Magura's heritage sites. It is a modest village visit rather than a museum. Literary travellers will find it a meaningful stop.
blocks: How to get there
From Magura town, go by bus or auto to Sreepur and ask for Majhail.
Good to know
Facilities are minimal; check locally about access.

madhumati-mohammadpur-ghat.desc: The Madhumati forms Magura's eastern edge and flows past Mohammadpur. Its ghats, including the old Nader Chand ghat, are places where ferries, fishing boats and bathers meet. Sandbanks appear in winter, while the monsoon brings brown, fast water. Sunset here after a day among the ruins is a fine end to the trip.
blocks: How to get there
A short ride east from Mohammadpur bazar to the riverbank.
Good to know
Avoid swimming; currents can be strong in the monsoon.

glance: 165 km to Magura by road, 4–6 hours by bus or car
sitaram-rajbari-mohammadpur.desc: Raja Sitaram Ray made Mohammadpur his capital around the turn of the 18th century and raised palaces, temples and large ponds such as Ram Sagar. After his fall the town declined, and today the palace and treasury buildings stand in ruins among village homes. The Dashabhuja temple and other shrines survive in varying states. The site is under attention from the Department of Archaeology.
blocks: How to get there
Bus or auto from Magura town to Mohammadpur upazila (about 25 km).
Good to know
Ruins are fragile; don't climb walls. A local guide helps find the scattered structures.

glance: 165 km to Magura by road, 4–6 hours by bus or car
sreepur-zamindar-bari.desc: The ruins lie about 15 km north of Magura town, a kilometre north of Sreepur upazila headquarters beside the boundary wall of Sreepur Mohila College. Local tradition says Sarada Ranjan Pal Chowdhury bought the estate from Nawab Alivardi Khan, and that his daughter married Udayaditya, son of Raja Pratapaditya of Jessore. People here believe Tagore drew on that story for Bou Thakuranir Haat. What survives is mainly the big arched gateway with guard rooms and a few walls; the government has never taken it over, and it is badly neglected.
blocks: How to get there
Take a bus or CNG from Magura town to Sreepur (about 15 km), then walk or take a rickshaw towards Sreepur Mohila College.
Good to know
The structure is unstable; look from outside and don't climb on it. Ask locals for the 'jomidar bari' near the women's college.

glance: 165 km to Magura by road, 4–6 hours by bus or car
siddheshwari-math-magura.desc: Siddheshwari Math stands in Atharokhada union of Magura Sadar, on the bank of the Nabaganga about 3 km from town. The place was once known as Kalikatala Shmashan, a cremation ground, and Banglapedia lists the math among the upazila's heritage sites. The old math building by the river makes a calm short trip from town, best in the soft light of late afternoon.
blocks: How to get there
From Magura town take an easy-bike or rickshaw to Atharokhada (about 3 km).
Good to know
It is a religious site; take off your shoes where asked and keep your voice down.
